reply_text:
I'm writing it now: a Python collector in futon3c/scripts and a small Elisp command that drives it.The collector works, and all four planted secrets were scrubbed. Next is the Emacs command:The batch test caught a bug: the Emacs context was read from inside `with-temp-file`, so it described the temp buffer and not your buffer. Fixing it:Committing both repos and updating the backlog entry:㊢ (built) **`M-x report-futon-bug`** works now, and it's autoloaded in your running Emacs. It asks for one line, then asks which agent to bell. Leave that empty to only write the report. The pieces:
- `futon3c/emacs/report-futon-bug.el`: the command. It collects the region, or the last 150 lines of the current buffer, plus `*Messages*` and `*Backtrace*`.
- `futon3c/scripts/futon_bug_report.py`: the collector. It adds Agency and futon1b health, the last 30 minutes of journal for futon3c, futon1b and emacs-graph, HEAD and dirty count for each futon repo, and zone-health. Then it **scrubs secrets** and writes `~/notes/futon-bugs/BUG-<stamp>-<slug>.md`. That's deliberately outside any repo, so nothing gets published by accident.
- If you name an agent, the **whole report goes in the bell** with `--mode work`, so the reader needs nothing else. The report includes a short "what the reader is asked to do" section: triage, reproduce, locate, propose a fix.

Commits: futon3c `4d79844f`, and futon0 `40696e4` for the autoload line in `contrib/futon-config.el` and the backlog entry.

㊬ (checked)
- Batch end-to-end run: about 24 seconds, mostly zone-health.
- Secrets planted in a fake buffer were scrubbed: GitHub token, Bearer, `*_TOKEN=`, JSON `access_token`, `sk-…`.
- The bell arguments are valid (`agency_send --dry-run`).
- The paren check and byte-compile are clean.
- No real bell has been sent yet.

Testing caught one bug: the command read its context from inside the temp buffer, so the report described the wrong buffer. That's fixed and retested.

🈹 (routing) I need to correct something I said earlier. The roster here *does* list remote proxies: `chi-claude-1` and `chi-codex-1` (metameso) and `ams-claude-1`. They'll appear in the prompt's completion list. zone-health still can't reach the federation peers' `/health`, though, so whether a bell to `chi-*` actually reaches metameso is untested. That's the "routing later" part.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-13
previous_reply_acts.text: ("report-futon-bug") Good idea. It's the same shape as `report-emacs-bug`: the tool gathers its own state, so you only supply a one-line description. I've added it to the alternative backlog (§5, futon0 `65fcd5f`) as an idea with a design sketch.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-13
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the sketch) `M-x report-futon-bug` asks for one line, typed or dictated, and gathers the rest:
- the region, or the tail of the current REPL buffer
- `*Messages*` and `*Backtrace*`
- recent journal lines for futon3c, futon1b and emacs-graph
- Agency and futon1b health, plus a zone-health summary
- the HEAD sha and dirty status of each futon repo
- host, time and Emacs version

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-13
previous_reply_acts.text: ("go to an agent on lucy or metameso") One constraint you'd hit today: zone-health shows the federation peers **unreachable from zone**, and the roster here lists no lucy or metameso agents. A bell to them would fail. So in a first version, the self-contained file would itself be the transport. It's committed to git, any host can pull it, and the bell goes to a local seat. Once federation is fixed (README-hardening §6), the same report could go straight to a remote agent.
